content: Oral tori are bony growths composed of compact bone that develop within the oral cavity, either along the palate or the mandible. A palatal torus, also known as torus palatinus, forms along the midline of the hard palate, while a mandibular torus, or torus mandibularis, arises on the lingual (inner) side of the mandible. The occurrence of tori is more common in women compared to men. These bony growths are typically associated with adulthood and are rarely observed before the age of 15. Palatal tori are particularly prevalent among Native American and Inuit populations. Treatment for oral tori is generally unnecessary unless they interfere with normal functions such as chewing or the fitting of prosthetic dental appliances.
